title: Chicken Fried Steak
subtitle: Tenderised beef steak in crispy seasoned crumb with white gravy
excerpt: Braising steak pounded thin, coated in seasoned flour and fried until deeply golden. Served with a creamy black pepper white gravy, straight from a Southern diner.
sourceNotes: Texas diner classic; chicken fried steak takes its name from the same frying technique used for fried chicken.

content.text: Chicken fried steak is a Texan diner dish of tenderised beef in a seasoned crumb crust. It gives a shatteringly crisp coating over tender, juicy meat. The white peppercorn gravy made in the same pan is the only accompaniment you need.

items.prepNote: about 150g each, pounded to 1cm thick with a meat mallet

content.text: Mix the flour, salt, black pepper, garlic powder, paprika and cayenne in the large bowl. Beat the eggs and milk together in a separate shallow bowl.
Dredge each steak in the seasoned flour, pressing it on firmly. Dip into the egg wash, then back into the flour. Press the coating firmly onto both sides.
Heat the oil in the cast-iron skillet over a medium-high heat. Test with a pinch of flour. It should sizzle briskly.
Fry the steaks two at a time for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply golden. Do not move them while they cook or the crust will lift off.
Rest the cooked steaks on a rack for 5 minutes. Pour off most of the oil, leaving about 2 tablespoons and all the browned bits in the pan.
Scatter the 3 tablespoons of flour over the oil in the pan and whisk over a medium heat for 1 minute.
Pour in the milk steadily, whisking all the time. Cook for 5 minutes until thick. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Plate the steaks and pour the white gravy over generously. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: The crust slides off during frying.
items.cause: The steaks were not dried before coating, or the coating was not pressed in firmly.
items.fix: Pat the steaks dry with kitchen paper before dredging. Press the flour coating in hard with your hands.

items.cause: The steak was not pounded thin enough.
items.fix: Pound each steak to an even 1cm all over. Any thick patches will be chewy.

items.cause: The milk went in too fast or the pan was too hot.
items.fix: Add the milk in a slow, thin stream and keep whisking constantly from the start.
